name: The Fool
theme: keep some lightness in the face of the unknown
upright: You may be standing at the threshold of a new stage. A small experiment will teach you more than waiting for the complete answer.
reversed: The line between impulse and avoidance is blurred. Notice whether you are following curiosity or escaping necessary preparation.
reflection: If you did not have to get it right the first time, how small could your first step be?

name: The Magician
theme: recombine the materials already in your hands
upright: You already have usable resources. The key is to choose one direction and let an idea become visible action for the first time.
reversed: There is plenty of information, but attention is scattered. Reduce your commitments, then check whether technique is replacing genuine intent.
reflection: Which resource you already possess could start the result you actually want to create?

name: The High Priestess
theme: let the answer take shape in quiet
upright: This is a time to observe rather than rush to declare. Treat recurring intuition as a clue, not a command.
reversed: You may be ignoring your own feelings or mistaking external expectations for an inner voice. Leave time for judgment without new input.
reflection: If nobody were watching, how would you describe what you truly know?

name: The Empress
theme: give what is growing the conditions it needs
upright: Creativity needs concrete living conditions. Rest, physical awareness and a steady rhythm will directly improve what you can produce.
reversed: Before caring for everyone else, check that your energy is not overdrawn. Excessive giving can become hidden control.
reflection: Which small, regular action would make this situation easier to grow?

name: The Emperor
theme: use clear boundaries to protect what matters
upright: Unclear rules are draining you. Define responsibility, time and limits, and the situation will become more manageable.
reversed: You may be mistaking control for stability. Check which rules still serve the goal and which are merely creating rigidity.
reflection: Which boundary would reduce the number of future repetitions?

name: The Hierophant
theme: find support inside a trustworthy framework
upright: Ask someone experienced or learn an established method first. A shared framework can reduce unnecessary trial and error.
reversed: An old rule may no longer fit. Not every difference needs rebellion, but you need to explain why you are choosing another path.
reflection: Which piece of experience should you inherit, and which rule needs to be reinterpreted?

name: The Lovers
theme: a choice also reveals the values you are unwilling to trade away
upright: The quality of a relationship depends on honest choice. Naming your real needs matters more than maintaining a smooth surface.
reversed: Mixed signals are increasing. Do not complete answers the other person has not given, and do not erase your own needs.
reflection: Which value in this choice are you least willing to exchange?

name: The Chariot
theme: point scattered energy toward one direction
upright: Progress comes from clear priorities. Give yourself one short-term goal and protect the time needed to pursue it.
reversed: Effort does not always equal movement. Check whether your goals conflict, then decide what can be set down for now.
reflection: What single result matters most for you to move forward over the next seven days?

name: Strength
theme: real strength allows emotion to exist
upright: Gentleness is not surrender. Steady, repeated small actions will handle intense feelings more effectively than forcing yourself to endure.
reversed: Self-criticism may be driving your effort. Reducing shame makes it easier to recover your capacity to act.
reflection: How would this situation change if you judged yourself a little less?

name: The Hermit
theme: step away from noise long enough to recalibrate
upright: You do not need more opinions as much as space to digest. Take the question on a walk, into writing or into intentional solitude.
reversed: Solitude may be turning into avoidance. Set a time to return to the conversation so reflection stays alive.
reflection: How much solitude do you need, and when will you return to the real relationship?

name: Wheel of Fortune
theme: the situation is changing, and your position needs to change with it
upright: The field is rearranging. Instead of clinging to the old outcome, notice where a new window of opportunity is opening.
reversed: A repeating pattern deserves attention. Separate chance from environment, then identify the part you can still influence.
reflection: Which old pattern can no longer continue through this change?

name: Justice
theme: separate facts from what you wish were true
upright: A decision needs complete information. Write down what you know, what you do not know and what you are currently assuming.
reversed: Standards may be inconsistent or responsibility may be shifting. Stop defending yourself long enough to face the necessary facts.
reflection: What would a fair observer remind you to confront?

name: The Hanged Man
theme: a pause can also be an active choice
upright: Not acting for a moment may reveal the most important part. Change your viewpoint and the result changes with it.
reversed: When waiting has lost its purpose, do not disguise delay as patience. Give the pause a deadline.
reflection: What are you willing to set down temporarily in order to see the real problem?

name: Death
theme: an ending makes room for a new structure
upright: A stage has completed its purpose. Acknowledging the ending does not invalidate what you invested in it.
reversed: Delaying goodbye prolongs the drain. You need to name clearly what should stop.
reflection: If you allowed this to end, what would be released?

name: Temperance
theme: let opposing needs gradually form a workable ratio
upright: Extreme plans do not fit you right now. Adjust the proportions until you find a more sustainable way forward.
reversed: Your rhythm may be out of balance. Do not only optimize efficiency; check whether rest and relationships are being squeezed.
reflection: How could two seemingly conflicting needs each retain a part of what they require?

name: The Devil
theme: seeing the bind makes it possible to loosen it
upright: A habit or relationship may be trading long-term freedom for brief certainty. Name the cost honestly before choosing again.
reversed: You are beginning to see the loop. Change the environmental cues rather than relying only on willpower.
reflection: What need is being served by the thing you are unwilling to release?

name: The Tower
theme: an unstable structure needs to become visible
upright: Sudden change has exposed a flaw in the old structure. Address safety and basic order before redesigning the larger plan.
reversed: You may sense change approaching while trying to preserve the surface. Small adjustments now can reduce the later impact.
reflection: Which fact can no longer be ignored?

name: The Star
theme: hope grows from repeatable, small repairs
upright: You are recovering a sense of the future. Keep one low-pressure long-term action so hope has somewhere concrete to land.
reversed: Confidence may be low, but you do not have to force optimism. Care for sleep, the body and one trustworthy connection first.
reflection: What small evidence reminds you that things are still slowly improving?

name: The Moon
theme: when things are unclear, separate feeling from fact
upright: The information is still incomplete. Record what you feel, but do not let fear write the entire conclusion.
reversed: The fog is beginning to clear. Rewrite vague worries as questions that can be tested, and anxiety will gain boundaries.
reflection: Which sentence you are worrying about has not actually been confirmed by facts?

name: The Sun
theme: honest expression brings light into the room
upright: This is a good time to make something public, confirmed or celebrated. Clear expression reduces misunderstanding.
reversed: The light is still there; temporary fatigue is covering it. Do not dismiss existing progress because your energy is low.
reflection: What progress deserves to be acknowledged instead of criticized?

name: Judgement
theme: past experience is asking for a more honest response
upright: You have enough information to choose. Review the past not to blame yourself, but to confirm the next step.
reversed: Self-doubt is delaying your response. Separate “I am not enough” from “I am not ready yet.”
reflection: If you no longer waited for approval, what would you respond to now?

name: The World
theme: completion is not an endpoint; it is a way to carry experience forward
upright: A cycle is closing. Acknowledge how far you have traveled before deciding what to carry into the next one.
reversed: You may be stuck at the final step. Identify the specific task that remains unclosed and give it a clear ending.
reflection: What concrete action would complete this chapter?
